name: coordinator-lifecycle-exclusivity
body:
Session lifecycle and exclusivity. `apg session start` launches the coordinator; `apg session end` releases the exclusive DB lock and the socket and exits cleanly. There is nothing to flush at session end: the coordinator performs each durable write itself, one commit per logical mutation (coordinator-single-writer), and applies each mutation's exact projection delta write-through as the mutation completes (write-through-projection, coordinator-buffer-derived-only) — the session only holds `db.lbug` open, it never defers a mutation's visibility. One session per worktree DB (a second start refuses or joins, never a second writer). A crash leaves a stale socket, which the next command/session cleans up (no live process behind it).

Mid-request session death: if the session dies after accepting a forwarded mutation but before committing/responding, the client MUST NOT silently fall back to the direct path — that could double-apply a mutation that already landed. Each forwarded mutation carries a client-generated request id; the coordinator records applied ids so a replay after reconnect is idempotent (apply-once). On a transport error the client reports the failure and the mutation id to the caller so the state can be reconciled, and only retries when the coordinator is reachable again and can confirm the id was not applied. The outcome is never hidden and never silently re-applied.

Read-only openers: `apg query` and every suite query tool open `db.lbug` read-only (`read_only(true)`, src/main.rs:963). While a session is live they keep working only by ROUTING through the live session (read-through, read-access-during-session): the session owns the DB and serves the read, so the routed reader takes no lock. A NON-routing reader that opens `db.lbug` directly during a live session is OUT of contract: lbug's contended open ERRORS ("Could not set lock … Resource temporarily unavailable") rather than waits, so there is no "contend and wait" fallback and the session must never be described as blocking a read. The only correct behaviours for a non-routing reader are to route via the tool or to be retried after the session ends (read-path-contract); a direct contended open is not a supported alternative.

A session is exclusive with `apg scan` and `apg project merge`, which replace `db.lbug` (the session ends — releasing the DB and socket — first, or those refuse while a session is live). Acceptance: start→mutations→end round-trips; a killed session leaves no process holding the DB and its stale socket is reclaimed; a mutation forwarded to a dying session is applied at most once and the client reports (never hides) the outcome; routed `apg query` / suite reads work while a session is live, while a non-routing direct open during a live session is out of contract (it routes or is retried after the session ends); scan/merge and a live session never contend.
